title: Cipher and Protocol
premise: Casper Oyelaran, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call they failed to save, receives a burner phone ringing with the voice of Marcus Vale—the man who died in that negotiation five years ago. The voice claims an attack is scheduled to look like an industrial accident at the Harrow Docks, orchestrated by the same shadowy network that rewrote the rules of Casper's last case and buried the truth. As Casper follows the phone's cryptic leads, they discover their mentor, Superintendent Ada Reyes, helped falsify the record of that fatal day, and that 'Marcus' may be alive, dead, or something in between—a test of loyalty engineered by people inside the force. The attack is real, but stopping it means exposing everyone Casper trusted, including themselves. In the end, Casper lets the truth go public at devastating personal cost, saves most of the dock workers, and walks away from the badge, carrying the knowledge that some protocols exist to protect power, not people.
about_author: Ivo Thornbury is the pen name of a former emergency services dispatcher turned novelist who spent a decade listening to the worst nights of strangers' lives. They write thrillers about institutions, secrets, and the people brave enough to break both.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Five years after the Kestrel Building failure, negotiator Casper Oyelaran trains rookies by day and drinks alone by night. A burner phone arrives in their mailbox with no return address. When it rings, the voice on the line is Marcus Vale—dead since the negotiation Casper still replays nightly. Beat: dread reawakened.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper reports the phone to Superintendent Ada Reyes, their mentor, who dismisses it as a cruel prank and orders them to hand it over. Casper complies—but keeps a recording. Flashback threads introduce the Kestrel case: three hostages, one shooter, one casualty. Beat: loyalty tested quietly.

chapters.title: Static and Ash
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The burner rings again: 'Harrow Docks. March the ninth. It will look like an accident.' Casper pulls old Kestrel files and finds pages redacted with signatures they don't recognize—including one that resembles Ada's. Beat: first crack in trust.

chapters.title: The Widow's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Nia Vale, Marcus's widow, running a small shipping brokerage near the docks. A stranger has been asking about her husband's old contracts. She keeps her own records, waiting years for someone to ask the right question. Beat: guarded hope.

chapters.title: Cold Board
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At a mandatory debriefing, Casper watches rookie negotiators rehearse the sanitized version of the Kestrel incident and realizes the official record has been rewritten—timeline shifted, calls missing. Someone inside curated the story. Beat: institutional betrayal dawning.

chapters.title: Voice Print
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper runs the recordings through a friend at a forensics lab. The voice matches Marcus Vale at ninety-four percent—but the background acoustics suggest a room that shouldn't exist in any police facility. Beat: uncanny confirmation.

chapters.title: Harrow at Low Tide
chapters.summary: POV Nia. Nia spots surveyors photographing the Harrow Docks' fuel storage depot—men with no permits and no company badges. She photographs them back and mails the film to the only address she trusts: Casper's. Beat: quiet defiance.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Hand
chapters.summary: POV Ada Reyes. Ada burns a document in her office fireplace and makes a call to someone called only 'the Accountant,' reporting that Casper received a package. She believes she is containing a threat to the force. Beat: antagonist revealed, sympathetic in her certainty.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Counting down from the date on the call, Casper maps the docks' infrastructure and finds the perfect accident scenario: a fuel line fault timed to a shift change. The plan is elegant, deniable, and designed to kill dozens while insuring someone else's millions. Beat: stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Old Frequencies
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper tracks the burner's signal history to a decommissioned police relay station—meaning whoever runs this has access to force infrastructure. The conspiracy isn't outside the walls; it built the walls. Beat: paranoia deepens.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knew
chapters.summary: POV Nia. Nia shares Marcus's private ledger: payments routed through her brokerage from a shell company called Protocol Holdings, dating back two years before his death. He was investigating, not participating—or so she believed. Beat: doubt about the dead.

chapters.title: The Accountant Calls
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A second voice joins the burner line—calm, bureaucratic, offering Casper a promotion and silence in exchange for standing down. It knows things only a colleague could know. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Rookie Mistake
chapters.summary: POV Theo Brandt, Casper's best trainee. Theo notices Casper acting strangely and, trying to help, mentions it to Ada. His loyalty becomes a weapon he doesn't know he's holding. Beat: innocence weaponized.

chapters.title: Surveillance State of Mind
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper realizes they're being followed—unmarked cars, a tail with police footwork. They go dark, using hostage-negotiation tradecraft to move through the city unseen. Beat: hunter becomes hunted.

chapters.title: The Kestrel Tapes
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In an evidence archive, Casper finds the original Kestrel recordings sealed under a false case number. Listening, they hear their own voice being fed false information through an earpiece during the fatal negotiation. They were managed, not failing. Beat: guilt transmuted into fury.

chapters.title: Ada's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada confronts the Accountant, demanding the operation end before Casper tears everything open. She learns her own role was larger than she admitted to herself—she didn't just cover up; she approved. Beat: self-deception collapsing.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The burner goes silent for two days. Casper, unraveling, nearly turns themselves in—until Nia calls: the surveyors are back at the docks, installing something. Beat: despair interrupted by purpose.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: POV Casper and Nia, alternating. Meeting in a rail yard, they compare ledgers and tapes. Either Marcus faked his death to run a sting, or someone is wearing his voice like a mask. Both possibilities demand the same next step: get inside Protocol Holdings. Beat: alliance forged.

chapters.title: The Broker's Door
chapters.summary: POV Nia. Nia reopens an old contract with Protocol Holdings as bait, requesting an in-person audit. She walks into their glass offices knowing she may not walk out. Beat: courage as calculation.

chapters.title: Glass House
chapters.summary: POV Nia. Inside Protocol Holdings, Nia recognizes the Accountant's face: Deputy Commissioner Ellery Voss, the man who once pinned a commendation on Marcus's coffin. She copies what she can and leaves a trace deliberately. Beat: audacity under pressure.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Ada summons Casper for a 'wellness review' that is clearly an interrogation. Casper plays the loyal officer, feeding Ada just enough doubt to make her hesitate when Voss asks for Casper's suspension. Beat: negotiation as survival.

chapters.title: March the Ninth
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The date arrives—and nothing happens. No attack, no movement. Casper realizes the date was a test or a decoy, and the real schedule lives somewhere in the ledger's numbers. Beat: rug pulled.

chapters.title: Cipher
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Decoding the ledger's payment dates against tide tables and shift rosters, Casper finds the true window: eleven days out, during a port authority inspection designed to keep emergency crews away. Beat: intellect as weapon.

chapters.title: The Voice Explains
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The burner rings at last. 'Marcus' admits he cannot prove who he is—only that he chose Casper because they never stopped asking why. He gives one verifiable fact about the Kestrel scene that was never in any file. Beat: faith over proof.

chapters.title: Grave Conditions
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper does the unthinkable: checks. What they find at the grave forces a choice between hope and sanity. The chapter ends without revealing what the headstone said. Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: Ada Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Confronted by Casper with the Kestrel tapes, Ada confesses everything: Voss ran Protocol Holdings, used the force as cover, and made her complicit one signature at a time. She agrees to testify—if she survives long enough. Beat: fall and redemption offered.

chapters.title: Loose Ends
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo, sent to watch Ada, witnesses two men entering her building. He faces the rookie's terrible arithmetic: obey orders or protect a person. He chooses wrong, then spends the chapter making it right. Beat: conscience under fire.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Ada, wounded but alive thanks to Theo, hides with Casper. She gives them the final piece: Voss's insurance policy—a kill switch of documents he keeps where no one would ever look. Beat: enemies becoming allies.

chapters.title: Protocol Zero
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The plan forms: expose Voss publicly at the moment the docks attack launches, forcing him to stand down or be destroyed. Every player takes a position. Casper volunteers for the one role they swore off—talking someone down. Beat: resolve crystallized.

chapters.title: The Longest Call
chapters.summary: POV Casper. On the night of the attack, Casper reaches Voss by phone and opens a negotiation with no authority, no backup, and total honesty as leverage. Beat: the negotiator's art at full power.

chapters.title: Pressure Drop
chapters.summary: POV Nia. At the docks, Nia and Theo work the physical side—evacuating workers under a pretext, buying minutes. A foreman who took Protocol money threatens to undo everything. Beat: tension in the machinery.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Said
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Mid-negotiation, the burner crackles: 'Marcus' speaks directly to Voss, reciting details only the real Marcus could know. Voss's composure fractures. Whether ghost or survivor, the voice does its work. Beat: supernatural-adjacent chill, human explanation pending.

chapters.title: Stand Down
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Voss, exposed on a live feed Ada arranged, aborts the attack rather than die a monster in public. But he offers Casper a final trade: the full truth of Kestrel in exchange for letting him vanish. Beat: climax pivot.

chapters.title: The Price of Truth
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper refuses the trade and releases everything—Kestrel tapes, Protocol files, Ada's testimony—to press and internal affairs alike. Voss is arrested at the docks among the workers he meant to burn. Beat: cost accepted.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Three workers were injured before the evacuation; none died. Theo testifies about his own failure and is suspended anyway. He visits Casper to say thank you and mean it. Beat: bittersweet accounting.

chapters.title: Ada's Hearing
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At the tribunal, Ada pleads guilty to falsification and names every name. Her sentence is light; her shame is not. She tells Casper she finally understands which protocol mattered. Beat: accountability without absolution.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Voice
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The answer comes quietly: Marcus survived Kestrel, disfigured and hidden, protected by Nia's silence, and spent five years building the case he couldn't bring home. The reunion is awkward, unfinished, and real. Beat: grief revised.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Offered a promotion to rebuild the negotiation unit, Casper declines. Some systems can be negotiated with; this one must be rebuilt from outside. They hand in the badge and keep the burner. Beat: identity chosen over institution.

chapters.title: Nia's Harbor
chapters.summary: POV Nia. The brokerage reopens under new ownership—hers, fully hers now. Marcus, changed beyond recognition, asks if there's room for him. She answers the way she answers everything: with a contract, honestly worded. Beat: love renegotiated.

chapters.title: Open Channel
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Months later, in a coastal town, Casper works crisis lines for civilians. The burner rings once more—an unknown voice, a new wrong, a request for help. Casper picks up. Beat: the ending as beginning; loyalty redirected toward truth.
